title: Kratom seizure leads to two arrests in Oxford - NewsBreak
text:
By none ,
1 days ago The Lafayette County Metro Narcotics Unit seized more than 500 units of kratom and other suspected narcotics Thursday during a search of an Oxford vape and tobacco store, resulting in the arrests of two people.
Agents began investigating Puffs Vape, Tobacco and Beer Store in the 100 block of Heritage Drive after receiving information about the alleged sale of illegal substances at the business. Investigators conducted a controlled purchase before obtaining a search warrant, according to the Metro Narcotics Unit.
During the search, agents recovered more than 500 units of kratom, along with THC cartridges, gummies and other suspected narcotics.
Kratom has been prohibited from possession, distribution and sale within the city of Oxford since 2019.
Yahya Mohamed Mosleh, 51, of Oxford, and Islam Mohamed, 18, of Oxford, were arrested and charged with possession of Schedule I controlled substances with intent to distribute.
The Metro Narcotics Unit did not say whether Thursday’s seizure was connected to the deaths of two University of Mississippi students earlier this week.
Kratom was found at both death scenes, according to law enforcement.
The two students, both male, were 18 and 20 years old. One died on campus and the other off campus.
The investigation into the deaths remains ongoing. Autopsies and toxicology testing are being conducted, with results expected over the next few weeks.
The Metro Narcotics Unit also said the business owner, Amer Alowdi, 40, was indicted in 2022 on a narcotics trafficking charge and fled the country before prosecution. Additional charges may be filed as the investigation continues.
“For years, our community has taken a clear position regarding these types of products. We have educated businesses, conducted compliance checks and worked aggressively to prevent illegal and potentially dangerous substances from being sold in Oxford. Despite those efforts, some individuals and businesses continue to put profit ahead of the safety of the people who live, work and attend school in our community.” — Lafayette County Metro Narcotics Unit
Authorities said the investigation remains active.
